newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Govt approves Kingstream steel plan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Govt approves Kingstream steel plan.

text.p: Kingstream Resources NL said on Thursday the Western Australian government had granted its approval for the A$1.4 billion mid-west iron and steel project.

"Plans to establish Western Australia's first-ever steel production plant have reached another milestone with cabinet giving its support to the terms of the State Agreement for the A$1.4 billion mid-west iron and steel project," Western Australian Resources Development Minister Colin Barnett was quoted as saying in a statement re-issued by Kingstream.
Kingstream shareholders are due to vote on a merger plan with Taiwan's An Feng Steel Co Ltd later this month.
The merged An Feng and Kingstream plan to develop the mid-west iron and steel project with annual capacity of 2.4 million tonnes of steel slab near the port of Geraldton, north of Perth.
The project still needs federal government approval through the Foreign Investment Review Board.
Barnett said studies into the suitability of Oakajee as a site for the project, and the feasibility of a deep water port, were continuing.
He said that Cabinet had agreed that the mid-west iron and steel project would be located at Oakajee provided the studies were positive for both the Government and An Feng Kingstream Steel.
Barnett said he intended to table the State Agreement in the next few weeks of Parliament and it would then be released to the stock exchange.
